Documentation → Monitoring & Analysis → Export to draw.io / SVG

Export a diagram to draw.io or SVG

Every diagram in the console — Architecture, Service Diagram, Concept Map, Plugin Studio app diagrams, the database ER diagram and Observability diagrams — downloads as a .drawio file you can edit in draw.io (diagrams.net), or as an SVG picture of exactly what is on screen.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view
📍 WhereThe draw.io and SVG buttons on each diagram's toolbar (POST /diagram-export/drawio; Observability › Diagrams uses /observability/diagrams/<id>/export.drawio)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • What does it do?
  • SVG: a picture of what is on screen

  • Troubleshooting
  • "There is nothing drawn to export yet."
  • "Exported. N item(s) could not be drawn in draw.io and were left out."
  • "the map is still loading" (Concept Map)
  • "Export to SVG failed: there is nothing drawn to export"
  • Export to draw.io failed: diagram too large to export

What is it?#

Every diagram in SATOM is drawn by the console itself (plain SVG, no diagram library), so each one has its own draw.io button that turns what is on screen into a .drawio file. Open the file in draw.io (diagrams.net, desktop or web) to annotate it, restyle it or put it in a design document. The file is a copy: editing it changes nothing in SATOM.

What does it do?#

The file holds the boxes, their text and colours, and the links between them, at the positions shown on screen:

Diagram Where the button is What the file holds
Architecture (/net-architecture/) toolbar, next to Trace a flow every element (label, kind, address, VLAN), every link, and the dashed gateway link of a network to its firewall
Service Diagram (/architecture/) toolbar, next to Fit zones, the Internet cloud and every device; an expanded device also exports each published service → server pool → back-end servers column
Concept Map (/map/) map tools, bottom right the hub and one table per concept with its pages as rows
Plugin Studio app diagram diagram toolbar, next to Fit every step (name, kind, key) and every arrow with its outcome word and colour — saved or not
Database → ER diagram ⤓ draw.io, next to ⤓ SVG one draw.io table per database table with every column, each foreign key drawn column to column with crow's-foot ends; inferred relationships dashed
Observability › Diagrams the editor toolbar and each diagram card the saved drawing, with each element's type

What is not in the file, on purpose: the live overlay (device state, hit counters, probe answers), a flow trace, the last-run colours of a Plugin Studio diagram and a step's parameters. They are SATOM state read on request; in draw.io they would be dead text.

SVG: a picture of what is on screen#

Next to draw.io, every diagram also has an SVG button (the ER diagram's is ⤓ SVG). Where the draw.io file is an editable copy of the drawing, the SVG is a picture: the layer you chose, the live overlay, a trace, highlights and search dimming are all in it.

  • The whole drawing, at 1:1. The zoom and pan do not matter: the picture is cropped to everything drawn.
  • Standalone. The console styles its diagrams with CSS, which does not travel in a file, so each element carries its own colours and fonts. The file opens on its own in a browser or an SVG editor, or inside a document.
  • On the page's canvas colour — light in the console, dark in Observability.
  • Left out: icon-font glyphs (the small icons on Observability elements need a font the file does not carry; the element type is still written under the label) and Observability's background dot grid.
  • In Plugin Studio the button is in the Diagram tab; on the Service Diagram switch to the Map view first (the List view has no drawing).
  • The SVG is made in your browser: it is not written to the audit log.

To import a draw.io, Visio, SVG, PDF or picture file as an editable diagram of its own, or to draw and publish diagrams, use Diagram Studio.

Permissions#

The button needs only the basic view access — any read permission grants it (monitoring.view, network.view, appliances.view, …) — and works in every ADOM: the export converts the drawing your page already shows and reads nothing else, so the page you export from has already decided what you may see. Every export is written to the audit log as diagram.export_drawio with the file name and its size.

How to use#

  1. Open the diagram and arrange it the way you want it on paper: on the Service Diagram expand the devices whose services you want and set the filters; on the ER diagram drag or re-layout the cards; in Observability, Save first (the export is the saved drawing).
  2. Press draw.io. The browser downloads <diagram name>.drawio.
  3. Open it in draw.io: File → Open from → Device, or drag it onto the draw.io window.

Example#

The ER diagram exports each table as a draw.io table: the header is the table name in its domain colour, each row is a column (PK id integer NOT NULL, FK appliance_id integer), and each foreign key is a crow's-foot connector from the column that holds it to the key it points at. In draw.io you can move the tables, delete the ones you do not need and the connectors stay attached to their columns.

Result#

  • A draw.io file opens with one page named after the diagram.
  • Observability round trip. A file exported from Observability › Diagrams imports back (Diagrams → Import) with the same element types, labels, addresses, positions and links: the type travels in the file as a satomType style key, which draw.io ignores.

Troubleshooting#

"There is nothing drawn to export yet."#

The diagram is empty (a new drawing, a filter that hides every device). Add elements or clear the filters.

"Exported. N item(s) could not be drawn in draw.io and were left out."#

A link whose end is not on the page (for example an element removed in another tab) cannot be drawn. The rest of the file is complete; the count tells you how many links were left out.

"the map is still loading" (Concept Map)#

The map is drawn the first time you switch to the map view. Wait for it to appear, then press draw.io again.

"Export to SVG failed: there is nothing drawn to export"#

The diagram is empty or not visible: open the tab or view that shows it (Plugin Studio Diagram tab, Service Diagram Map view) and try again.

Export to draw.io failed: diagram too large to export#

The description of the diagram is over 8 MB, or has more than 5,000 elements or 10,000 links. Filter the diagram down (zones, devices, a smaller drawing) and export the parts.
